language.label: Language
language.previewNote: If you spot a wrong translation, please {url} and we will fix it.

tieBreak.label: Tie-break
tieBreak.description: Sets where a mod that no other mod pins starts from. Rebuild ranks those mods by name and ignores your current order, so expect most mods to move the first time you rebuild a list RimSort produced. Preserve current starts each mod from its position in ModsConfig.xml, moving as few mods as possible.

useImportedPairs.label: Use imported pair rules
useImportedPairs.description: Let RimSort/SteamDB "load before/after" rules affect ordering. On by default — most imported pairs restate evidence the sorter already enforces on its own. A rule you set yourself is never affected by this toggle.

useImportedPlacements.label: Use imported placement rules
useImportedPlacements.description: Let RimSort/SteamDB "load first/last" placements pin a mod's tier. On by default — nothing in a mod's own files can say "load me last".

enforceSoft.label: Enforce Soft-strength edges
enforceSoft.description: These edges come from lazily-resolved references to {assemblyRef}. Off by default: enforcing them can move noticeably more mods from their current order than leaving them advisory.

enforceAwareness.label: Enforce Awareness-strength edges
enforceAwareness.description: These edges come from {edgeKinds} hints — evidence that the mods interact, not an ordering fact. Off by default: they are far more common than Soft edges, so enforcing them is far more disruptive to the order.

enforceInferred.label: Enforce Inferred-strength edges
enforceInferred.description: These edges are {edgeKinds}: the analyzer's own heuristic conclusions that two mods interact, not just a presence signal like Awareness. On by default: unlike Soft and Awareness edges, the analyzer has already concluded these are ordering facts, so leaving them advisory-only would discard that evidence.

network.heading: Internet access
network.recoveredWarning: Your app settings file couldn't be read, so internet access is off until you save settings again.

allowNetwork.label: Allow internet access
allowNetwork.description: The master switch for everything Rimmerge sends over the internet, automatic or manual. It only ever contacts two GitHub hosts — api.github.com for update checks and raw.githubusercontent.com for rule-database refreshes — and never your local network. Off skips every request before any address is built or connection opened. Applies to this whole app, on this computer, whichever RimWorld install you open.

autoRefreshRuleDatabases.label: Refresh rule databases automatically
autoRefreshRuleDatabases.description: Once a day, at launch, fetch the enabled rule databases the Rule databases card lists — never the Steam Workshop database, which only ever refreshes when you click Refresh.

checkForUpdates.label: Check for updates
checkForUpdates.description: Once a day, at launch, check whether a newer Rimmerge has been released.

suggestMergeWhenClean.label: Suggest merging clean overrides
suggestMergeWhenClean.description: When two mods change different fields of the same def, suggest merging them instead of keeping the load-order winner. Merged defs are written to the merge mod on apply.

showDanglingDefReferences.label: Show dangling def reference findings
showDanglingDefReferences.description: Flag a name written at a recognized reference site (e.g. a research prerequisite, a stat offset key) that no active def of any type actually has. Off by default — this can produce a meaningful number of false positives on a large install (for example a self-identifying field mistaken for a cross-reference). Never changes the load order.

welcome.title: Welcome to Rimmerge
welcome.body:
Rimmerge can contact GitHub once a day, when it starts:
- to check whether a newer Rimmerge has been released (api.github.com);
- to download updated rule databases — the community load-order rules and Rimmerge's own rules file (raw.githubusercontent.com). Updates are stored locally; they change your load order only when you choose to import them.

It sends nothing about you, your mods, or your install — only a plain request that GitHub sees your IP address for. The large Steam Workshop database is never downloaded automatically, only when you click Refresh.

layerPhrase.declaredOverride: your own explicit override of the author's declaration

relationExplanation.presenceOnly: this only tests whether a mod is present, not its load position
relationExplanation.patchTargetsDef: patches apply to the merged def document after every mod's defs are loaded, regardless of load order
relationExplanation.parentTemplate: unreachable: a ParentName edge is a load-time ordering fact (Hard), never advisory
relationExplanation.usesType: the type is resolved across every loaded assembly regardless of load order
relationExplanation.patchSelectsInjectedNode: the selected node may already exist another way (written inline, injected by more than one active mod, or injected by the selecting mod's own patch), or lies deeper than the analyzer indexes to check — so this isn't a proven load-order requirement
relationExplanation.patchRemovedNode: the analyzer infers this from patch content: one mod removes a node another mod also patches, and the remover must load last or the other patch finds nothing left to touch — not an author's own declared load order, so it yields when a declaration or placement disagrees
relationExplanation.retextureAfterOwner: the analyzer infers this from a shared texture path: a texture-only retexture pack must load after the content mod it reskins, or its replacement is overwritten by the content it's meant to retexture — not an author's own declared load order, so it yields when a declaration or placement disagrees
relationExplanation.defOverrideAfterOrigin: the analyzer infers this from template/def-count evidence: a mod that also ships a def belonging to another mod's own namespace must load after that namespace's owner, or its override lands under the origin's own definition instead of on top of it — not an author's own declared load order, so it yields when a declaration or placement disagrees
relationExplanation.patchInvalidatesPredicate: the analyzer infers this from patch content: a Replace/Remove rewrites or deletes a node another mod's own xpath predicate reads, and the predicate-reading op must load first or its own predicate no longer matches — not an author's own declared load order, so it yields when a declaration or placement disagrees
relationExplanation.patchRemovedNodeCosmetic: the analyzer infers this from patch content, but the final defs are identical either order here — only which mod's own op logs the failure changes — so it's weaker evidence than an author's own declared load order and yields when a declaration or placement disagrees
relationExplanation.replaceDiscardsAddition: the analyzer infers this from patch content: a Replace swaps in a whole new node, silently discarding whatever an earlier addition wrote into it, so the addition must load after the replace or its own content is lost with no log line at all — not an author's own declared load order, so it yields when a declaration or placement disagrees
relationExplanation.interactionEvidence: this is evidence the mods interact, not an ordering fact the loader itself needs

edgeDroppedInferred.patchRemovedNode: {after} removes a node that {before} also patches; {after} must load after {before} or {before}'s own patch would find nothing left to touch. The analyzer inferred this from patch content, not from either mod's own declared load order.
edgeDroppedInferred.retextureAfterOwner: {after} is a texture-only retexture pack sharing a texture path with {before}'s own content; {after} must load after {before} or its replacement texture is overwritten by the content it's meant to reskin. The analyzer inferred this from the shared texture path, not from either mod's own declared load order.
edgeDroppedInferred.defOverrideAfterOrigin: {before} owns the template or def family this override belongs to; {after} also ships a copy of it and must load after {before} so the override lands on top of the origin's own definition. The analyzer inferred this from template/def-count evidence, not from either mod's own declared load order.
edgeDroppedInferred.patchInvalidatesPredicate: {after} replaces or removes a node that {before}'s own patch selects through a predicate; {after} must load after {before} or {before}'s own predicate would no longer match. The analyzer inferred this from patch content, not from either mod's own declared load order.
edgeDroppedInferred.replaceDiscardsAddition: {before} replaces a node that {after} also adds content into; {after} must load after {before} or its own addition is silently discarded when {before}'s Replace swaps in a whole new node, with no log line at all. The analyzer inferred this from patch content, not from either mod's own declared load order.

rationale.edgeDroppedCosmetic: cosmetic: the final defs are identical in either order; only which log line appears changes
rationale.keepEdgeInCycle: Keep this edge; the sorter will drop the next-weakest edge in the cycle instead.
rationale.reorderOverridingEdgeWinner: Force this mod's own order instead, overriding the winner.
rationale.edgeDroppedWithWinner: {after} must load before {before} instead: {layerPhrase} says so ({detail}).
rationale.edgeDroppedSoftOrAwareness: Dropping a soft or awareness-only edge to break a cycle rarely changes behavior.
rationale.edgeDroppedDeclared: An author-declared edge had to be dropped to break a cycle.
rationale.edgeDroppedHard: A hard (load-time) edge had to be dropped to break a cycle: the mods are genuinely in conflict.
rationale.removeDependentModBrokenOrder: Remove the dependent mod from the active list instead of accepting a broken load order.
rationale.reorderOppositeOfRelation: Force the opposite order the relation implies, as a user decision.
rationale.declarationOverridden: {declaredAfter} is declared to load after {declaredBefore} ({detail}), but {layerPhrase} says otherwise: {byAfter} loads after {byBefore} instead ({byDetail}).
rationale.anyOfNoCandidate: No candidate could satisfy this constraint without closing a cycle.
rationale.forceAnyOfCandidateAcceptingCycle: Force this candidate, accepting whatever cycle results elsewhere.
rationale.anyOfChosenAlreadyBefore: The chosen candidate already loads before the dependent mod today.
rationale.anyOfAlternativeCandidate: An alternative candidate could also satisfy this constraint.
rationale.anyOfUniqueMaxDependents: The chosen candidate is the uniquely most-depended-on mod among the candidates.
rationale.anyOfSmallestId: Chosen by the smallest id among otherwise-tied candidates.
rationale.ruleOverruledLongerCycle: {rulePhrase} had to be dropped to break a longer cycle among several mods.
rationale.ruleOverruledByWinner: {rulePhrase} was overruled: {layerPhrase} says {before} loads after {after} instead ({detail}).
rationale.reorderOverridingRuleWinner: Force this rule's own order instead, overriding the winner.
rationale.promoteRuleDespiteOverruled: Keep this rule as your own decision, so it survives even though it stays overruled.
rationale.promotePlacementDespiteOverruled: Keep {placementPhrase} placement as your own decision, so it survives even though it's overruled.
rationale.dropRuleOverrulingPlacement: Drop the rule that overruled this placement, keeping {modId} {placementPhrase}.
rationale.enforceRelationAsUserDecision: Enforce this relation explicitly as a user decision.

placementOrderingOverridden.loadsAfter: {pinned} is pinned {placementPhrase}, but {modId} must load after it anyway: {layerPhrase} ({detail}).
placementOrderingOverridden.loadsBefore: {pinned} is pinned {placementPhrase}, but {modId} must load before it anyway: {layerPhrase} ({detail}).

rationale.placementPromotesDependents: {modId} is pinned {placementPhrase}; {count} other mod is attributed to it as promoted past its own tier boundary too{sample} | {modId} is pinned {placementPhrase}; {count} other mods are attributed to it as promoted past its own tier boundary too{sample}
rationale.forceDefOverrideWinner: Force a specific owner's def to win regardless of load order.
rationale.defOverrideWinnerDeclaresRelation: The winning mod explicitly declares a load-order relation to every other owner.
rationale.defOverrideLoneNonVanillaOwner: Exactly one active mod overrides this vanilla def; nothing else contests it.
rationale.defOverrideShadowsFramework: A leaf mod is quietly shadowing a shared framework's def.
rationale.defOverrideUnexplained: Multiple mods define this def with no strong signal explaining the override.
rationale.mergeUnexplainedDefOverride: Merge field by field instead of accepting one owner's def outright.
rationale.mergeShadowsFrameworkFieldByField: Merge field by field; keep the framework's values where the leaf mod didn't change them.
rationale.forcePatchCollisionWinner: Force one mod's patch to apply exclusively.
rationale.patchCollisionAdditive: Every contributing patch only adds to the target; order doesn't change the outcome.
rationale.patchCollisionContested: At least one contributing patch mutates the target; load order decides the outcome.
rationale.patchCollisionWinnerDeclaresRelation: {winner} declares it loads after {others}, so its change to '{field}' is kept as written.
rationale.mergeContestedPatchCollision: Merge field by field instead of letting load order decide the whole def.
rationale.patchWillFailRemovedBy: {remover}'s own operation removes the node {modId}'s operation at '{xpath}' targets, loading before it in the order this was checked against.
rationale.reorderBeforeRemover: Load {modId} before {remover}, so its operation runs while the node still exists.
rationale.patchWillFailNotYetInjected: {modId}'s operation at '{xpath}' targets a node {injector} injects, but {injector} loads after it in the order this was checked against.
rationale.reorderAfterInjector: Load {modId} after {injector}, so its operation finds the node once injected.
rationale.patchWillFailDeadTarget: {modId}'s operation at '{xpath}' targets a node the winning owner's own resolved structure never has, regardless of load order — no reorder fixes this.
rationale.patchWillFailUnknownCause: {modId}'s operation at '{xpath}' is predicted to fail; the cause couldn't be classified.
rationale.brokenInheritance: This `ParentName` reference doesn't resolve the way the child's own element type expects — the def loads with content missing or wrong. Report this to the referencing mod's author.
rationale.danglingDefReference: This name resolves to no active def of any type — {cause}.{soundCaveat} Cross-references resolve after every mod's defs and patches have loaded, so this never depends on load order.
rationale.danglingDefReferenceSoundCaveat: This looks like a sound reference — a missing `SoundDef` logs a warning and silently falls back to an undefined sound rather than failing to load.
rationale.discardedAdditionDeliberate: {replacer} declares it loads after {adder} and replaces '{path}': {adder}'s own addition at '{adderPath}' is discarded on purpose.
rationale.forceTextureWinner: Force one mod's texture to win.
rationale.copyTextureIntoMergeMod: Copy this mod's texture file into the merge mod, independent of load order.
rationale.textureOverrideCosmetic: A texture override is cosmetic and browsable in-game; it never blocks.
rationale.forceTemplateRegistrationWinner: Force this mod's registration to apply to every one of the template's own children, regardless of load order.
rationale.duplicateTemplateNameExplanation: {ownerCount} mod registers this template name; each child independently inherits from whichever registration loads nearest at or before it. If none does, it falls back to a vanilla registration, or failing that to the registration from the mod that loads first in the load order, so different children can resolve to different mods. | {ownerCount} mods register this template name; each child independently inherits from whichever registration loads nearest at or before it. If none does, it falls back to a vanilla registration, or failing that to the registration from the mod that loads first in the load order, so different children can resolve to different mods.
rationale.keyedTranslationCollision: These two mods share {keyCount} translation key; the last-loaded one wins. | These two mods share {keyCount} translation keys; the last-loaded one wins each one.
rationale.soundOverrideCosmetic: A sound override is cosmetic and audible in-game; it never blocks.
rationale.forceSoundWinner: Force one mod's sound to win.
rationale.missingTexturePath: This texture path is shipped by no active mod — the game will show a magenta placeholder in its place.
rationale.undecodableTexture: This .dds file won't decode — the base game shows the bad-texture placeholder in its place.
rationale.contributesNothing: {modId} contributes nothing observable under this order: it ships no assembly, every def it owns is overridden by a later copy, every texture and translation it ships is overridden, and every patch operation it has either fails to apply or never runs — disabling it changes nothing in-game and saves its load cost.
rationale.undeclaredTypeDependency: {user} uses a type from {provider}'s assembly but declares no dependency on it.
rationale.pinRelationExplicitly: Pin the relation explicitly as a load-order rule.
rationale.runtimePatchCollisionLastPatcher: {ownerCount} mod patches {targetType}.{targetMethod}; {last} loads last today, so its patch runs last. | {ownerCount} mods patch {targetType}.{targetMethod}; {last} loads last today, so its patch runs last.
rationale.forceRuntimePatchLastWinner: Force this mod's patch to run last, regardless of load order.
rationale.transpilerCollision: {ownerCount} mod rewrites {targetType}.{targetMethod}'s IL with a runtime-patch transpiler; the order they run in can decide whether a later one's own pattern still matches. Most such collisions are harmless — if one of these mods logs a patching error, state the working order with `rimmerge rule set-pair`. | {ownerCount} mods each rewrite {targetType}.{targetMethod}'s IL with a runtime-patch transpiler; the order they run in can decide whether a later one's own pattern still matches. Most such collisions are harmless — if one of these mods logs a patching error, state the working order with `rimmerge rule set-pair`.
rationale.duplicateAssemblyFirstLoadedWins: More than one active mod ships an assembly of this name; the first-loaded copy wins at runtime.
rationale.removeDuplicateAssemblyCopy: Remove one of the duplicate copies from the active list.
rationale.likelyDuplicateMod: These two mods share a large number of identical defs with no declared relation between them.
rationale.removeLikelyDuplicateModA: Remove one of the likely-duplicate mods from the active list.
rationale.removeLikelyDuplicateModB: Remove the other likely-duplicate mod from the active list.
rationale.missingModNotInstalled: This mod is active in ModsConfig.xml but isn't installed; RimWorld drops unknown ids anyway.
rationale.keepMissingModId: Keep the id in ModsConfig.xml in case the mod reappears.
rationale.missingDependencyNotEnforced: A declared dependency isn't active; RimWorld only warns about this, it doesn't enforce it.
rationale.incompatiblePair: These mods declare each other incompatible.
rationale.removeIncompatibleModA: Remove one of the incompatible mods from the active list.
rationale.removeIncompatibleModB: Remove the other incompatible mod from the active list.
rationale.unsupportedVersionOftenWorks: This mod doesn't list the active game version as supported; it often still works anyway.
rationale.undeclaredHardDependencyHonored: The sorter already honors this hard (load-time) edge even though the author never declared it.
rationale.pinRelationExplicitlyAnyway: Pin the relation explicitly as a load-order rule anyway.
rationale.lazyReferenceViolatedJitResolved: This lazily-resolved assembly reference isn't honored by the current order, but it resolves at JIT time after every assembly is loaded, so load order doesn't actually affect it.

nearMissModReference.findModName: This FindMod name '{written}' resolves to no active or installed mod, but closely resembles the active mod '{candidateName}' — possibly a typo. Report this to the referencing mod's author.
nearMissModReference.mayRequireId: This MayRequire id '{written}' resolves to no active or installed mod, but closely resembles the active mod '{candidateName}' — possibly a typo. Report this to the referencing mod's author.

rationale.mergeCompleteNothingToMerge: the game applies these contributions in sequence to a single value; nothing to merge
rationale.mergeLeadDefOverrideCombine: The mods change different fields; merging would combine both.
rationale.mergePromotedPatchCollisionKeepsBoth: The mods change different fields; merging keeps both.
rationale.mergeStructuralGuard: {field} differs between owners — field-level merging is unsafe; confirm the load-order winner
rationale.mergeFieldsNeedChoice: Merge, {unresolved} field needs a choice. | Merge, {unresolved} fields need a choice.
rationale.identicalCopiesOrderIrrelevant: identical copies; order cannot change the outcome
rationale.notAddressedByPatch: Not addressed by this patch; load order decides as today.
